status: Rejected server cipher-policy CPU/throughput screen; selected SessionIO remains unchanged
decision_rationale: All three ordinary throughput medians regress with the same fixed client binaries: private -23.45752%, room -11.83753%, mixed -15.49692%. Candidate server CPU seconds and CPU per verified delivery also rise. All remaining controls passed, but functional delivery success does not offset whole-workload regression. No Ring compact-ChaCha follow-on will be implemented from this screen; full throughput and memory parity remains unmet.

preflight_failure_preserved.explanation: V1 baseline traffic passed, but benchmark_transport.prepare reset RUST_LOG to war_relay=info, leaving no suite debug logs. Diagnostic assertion failed before any ordinary case. This is a logging/controller failure, not a cipher failure; all V1 timings excluded.

limits: No Ring key representation changes or new memory measurements; cipher choice alone does not prove a memory saving.
Fixed client binaries negotiate a different cipher, which can change client CPU cost. Both endpoint CPU counters are reported; do not attribute every throughput change solely to server computation.
Debug suite diagnostics are separate and excluded from medians. All30 ordinary/control attempts are preserved including failures.
V2 diagnostics set debug logging only after original benchmark_transport.prepare, restore it finally, and leave ordinary preparation unchanged.
Round-trip percentiles are histogram upper bounds. Datagram unreceived counts are within the observation window, not proof of network loss.
This screen does not establish native WebSocket throughput/memory parity, browser compatibility, complete kernel-memory accounting, or loss/bulk freshness acceptance.
